title: At 4am on this day, Indian troops crossed into Hyderabad - and ended 224 years of Nizam rule in five days.
sources: Wikipedia - Indian annexation of Hyderabad (Operation Polo, 13-18 September 1948)
Vajiram & Ravi - Operation Polo 1948, Annexation of Hyderabad
Shankar IAS Parliament - 77th Anniversary of Operation Polo
caption:
At 4am on this day, Indian troops crossed into Hyderabad - and ended 224 years of Nizam rule in five days.

Hyderabad State, ruled by the Nizam, had refused to join the Indian Union after independence - its own private army, the Razakars, was carrying out mass violence against the population. On September 13, 1948, Indian forces entered at 4am.

By September 17-18, Hyderabad's forces surrendered and the Nizam capitulated. What decades of political stalemate couldn't resolve, five days of decisive action did - integrating the largest princely state left outside the Union.

Every princely state that joined the Union, one negotiation or one operation at a time, is part of why India today is one country instead of a patchwork of five hundred. Hyderabad was the hardest holdout - and still came together.
